title: Normal brain patterning needs the Vmem difference between neural tube and lateral tissue

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Normal brain patterning needs the Vmem difference between neural tube and lateral tissue

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In Xenopus brain development, it is the spatial contrast of Vmem that matters: depolarizing the neural tube region or hyperpolarizing the lateral regions both cause brain defects, because the precise differential bioelectric state induces the balance of proliferation, apoptosis and gene expression needed to build a normal brain.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The spatial patterning is crucial, as both depolarization of the middle region, or hyperpolarization of the lateral regions, both cause brain defects—it is the precise differential bioelectric state that induces the required balance of proliferation, apoptosis, and gene expression to build a normal brain28,48.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › BETSE model identifies HCN2 channel as a repair reagent”. Scope: Neural tube and surrounding ectoderm of Xenopus neurula-stage embryos

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The contrast hypothesis is explicit and can be distinguished from absolute-voltage alternatives using reciprocal perturbations. Published studies may cover parts of this design, but no open, unified embryo-level dataset with all four readouts is identified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare brain morphology, proliferation, apoptosis, and marker expression after independently reducing neural-tube hyperpolarization or hyperpolarizing lateral tissue, and test whether defect severity tracks spatial Vmem contrast rather than absolute voltage.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Absolute voltage and spatial contrast may be correlated.

The required spatially targeted perturbations are scattered across studies.

fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.74
data existence: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decision rule is a pair of anatomical outcomes keyed to where Vmem is moved, and the claim's scope is exactly the Xenopus neurula. Those experiments were published as measurements, so they can be compiled, but they are not an open reanalysis file. Ion confounds and single-lab scoring keep the test informative rather than clean. Coverage matches the stated species and stage only as far as those papers go.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score major brain morphology after two perturbations that flatten the same spatial Vmem contrast: depolarize the neural tube, or hyperpolarize the lateral ectoderm. Defects in both arms, and a spared brain when the contrast is preserved, would support the contrast claim; a defect in only one arm would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The evidence is from one laboratory and one species.

Depolarizing and hyperpolarizing reagents also change intracellular ions and pH.

The two perturbations live in earlier papers' figures, not a downloadable landmark or voltage table.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.8
